rationale: Correct Terra-Gen to preserve its full ownership history and current 50/50 legal ownership. Regulatory and company sources establish Igneo's GDIF chain at 50% and Masdar at 50%, with ArcLight, Global Infrastructure Partners and Energy Capital Partners as former sponsors. Pantheon Infrastructure Plc committed to a Terra-Gen-specific co-investment through an Igneo-managed vehicle in June 2026, but no public source establishes closing, funding, a stake or a reduction of Igneo's 50%; it is therefore recorded only as a signed pending incoming transaction. No later corporate ownership change or exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

beforeImage.name: Terra-Gen
beforeImage.subsector: Utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage
beforeImage.description: Terra-Gen develops, constructs, owns, and operates utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage projects in the United States. Its end markets include utilities, corporate offtakers, and wholesale power markets that require large-scale renewable generation and storage capacity. The operating model is asset-heavy and development-to-ownership because the business originates, finances, builds, and operates physical generation and storage assets with a mix of contracted and market-based revenues. Public disclosures describe a portfolio concentrated in California with additional assets in Texas and New York, including roughly 3.8 GW of operating capacity and 5.1 GWh of storage across about 30 sites, plus a development pipeline exceeding 12 GW. Terra-Gen was formed in 2007, Igneo made its initial investment through Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund (GDIF) in December 2020, and Masdar closed the acquisition of a 50 percent stake in October 2024 while Igneo retained its 50 percent interest.

afterImage.name: Terra-Gen
afterImage.subsector: Utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage
afterImage.description: Terra-Gen develops, owns and operates utility-scale wind, solar and battery-storage assets across the United States. Public disclosures through July 2026 describe approximately 4.2 GW of gross operating capacity, 5.6 GWh of storage, 34 sites and a roughly 16 GW development pipeline. Terra-Gen Power Holdings II, LLC is the parent platform, Terra-Gen, LLC is the operating business and individual project SPVs remain subordinate assets. Current legal ownership is 50% through Igneo Infrastructure Partners' Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund chain and 50% through Masdar's acquisition chain. ArcLight formed the platform in 2007, Global Infrastructure Partners invested in 2009, Energy Capital Partners acquired it in 2015 and used a 2021 continuation vehicle for its retained 50% before Masdar closed its purchase on October 1, 2024. Pantheon Infrastructure Plc committed to a Terra-Gen-specific co-investment through an Igneo-managed vehicle in June 2026, but closing, funding, the security and stake were not publicly confirmed; Igneo remains recorded at 50% pending evidence. No later corporate ownership change or signed exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: ArcLight formed Terra-Gen from renewable-generation assets acquired from Caithness.
Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to invest through convertible preferred securities representing up to a 40% interest in Terra-Gen.
Energy Capital Partners III acquired Terra-Gen, ending the ArcLight and Global Infrastructure Partners ownership periods.
Igneo's Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund closed an initial 40% investment and increased its Terra-Gen interest to 50%; ECP transferred its retained 50% into a continuation vehicle.
Masdar announced an agreement to acquire Energy Capital Partners' 50% Terra-Gen stake while Igneo retained its 50% interest.
Masdar completed its 50% acquisition from Energy Capital Partners, leaving Terra-Gen owned 50% by Masdar and 50% by Igneo's GDIF chain.
Pantheon Infrastructure announced a Terra-Gen-specific co-investment commitment through an Igneo-managed vehicle; closing, funding and the resulting stake were not publicly confirmed.
